title: legionctl config set
description: Replace the stored controller document with what is on stdin. Acceptance is decided by ANCESTRY, not by revision order: the push is taken when the hash the machine holds is the pushed hash (noop) or appears in the pushed document's lineage (fast-forward). A pushed hash that appears in the HELD lineage means the pusher is behind (stale-revision); anything else is real divergence (controller-conflict, divergent true) and stops at a person. A different setup id needs --replace, which is a human decision and is never sent automatically.

allOf.description: A push that landed says which of the three things it did.

Every refusal says what the machine is still holding, in the terms that decide what the client does next. A document refusal names the held copy and its lineage; a lock refusal names the operation in the way.
Divergence is the one thing the client cannot infer from the code alone: a controller-conflict is either two setups or two branches of one, and only the second is a merge.
noop means nothing was written, so the hash the machine holds is the hash that was pushed.
replaced is only ever the answer to an explicit --replace.

replaced.description: True when --replace was given and an existing copy under a different identity was overwritten.

current.description: What the machine is still holding after a refusal.

action.description: stored: the document was written (a first copy or a fast-forward). noop: the machine already holds exactly these bytes, so nothing was written and a retried push is safe. replaced: --replace was given and a copy under a different setup id was overwritten. Present only on success: a refusal wrote nothing and has no outcome to name.

divergent.description: Set on a refusal. True when neither side descends from the other, which is the case a person has to merge; false when the pusher is simply behind, which the pusher fixes by fetching.

lineage.description: The lineage of the document now stored, echoed back so a client can confirm what it published without another read.

conflict.description: Set when the refusal is the machine-wide operation lock rather than anything about the document: a setup change during a running update could be read half-written by that update.
